gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a working 10GbE copper link costs on each box: the DXP4800 GT gets one for $559.99 with nothing else to buy, but the UniFi UNAS Pro 4 has no 10GbE RJ45 port and its $499 sticker becomes $614 once you add Ubiquiti's listed $549 surcharge-included price and its $65 SFP+ to RJ45 adapter.
standout_why: Our own current page (dealectric.com/best-4-bay-nas-10gbe-under-700) divides sticker price by port count: GT $329.99, UNAS Pro 4 $249.50, TS-432X $659. It has no adapter cost, no surcharge and no power figure, and the GT price it uses is stale ($659.99, now $559.99). ChooseCompute's best-4-bay page lists prices and cost per usable TB but no watts, energy cost or cost per port. The ChatGPT answers say the TS-432X needs SFP+ gear, but none puts a price on it. None of the answers mention the UNAS Pro 4 at all.
decides: This confirms the DXP4800 GT as the cheapest working native 10GbE under $700 at $559.99 ($280 per port). It also stops the UNAS Pro 4 from winning on its $499 headline: on an RJ45 network one 10GbE link costs $614 at Ubiquiti's surcharge-included price, or $564 before the surcharge. The Pro 4 only stays cheapest ($512 to $562 with a $13 DAC) for a shopper who already owns an SFP+ switch. The same caveat applies to the TS-432X: it ships with no SFP+ module, so $659 is not the price of a working link. Running the 10GbE link on the DXP4800 Plus costs about $10 a year in extra power.
